newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Four Asians die in Bahrain shop blaze.
newsitem.headline: Four Asians die in Bahrain shop blaze.

text.p: Four Asians died and a fifth is in critical condition after an arson attack on a shop in the Bahraini capital Manama on Friday, an interior ministry official said.
The official, quoted by the Gulf News Agency, said the four died from smoke inhalation.
Shi'ite Moslems have launched sporadic attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Friday's blaze was the latest in a series of fires to hit the island, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre, this week. Bahraini officials say some were premeditated.
Two fires destroyed three Asian-owned shops in Manama late on Wednesday and another gutted a flat in a Manama district earlier in the day.
On Tuesday fires destroyed two shops in the Shi'ite village of Khamis and on Monday firefighters were seen battling blazes in Sanabis village and nearby areas.
The latest deaths raise to more than 30 the number of people killed in the Gulf Arab state in more than two years of anti-government unrest.
Seven Bangladeshi workers died in March 1996 when suspected arsonists set a restaurant ablaze on the small island of Sitra, linked with Manama by a three km (1.8 miles) causeway.
